newsitem.title: INDIA: Monsoon delays, power cut hit India Grasim output.
newsitem.headline: Monsoon delays, power cut hit India Grasim output.

text.p: India's Grasim Industries said on Tuesday its production of viscose staple fibre (VSF) in the six months to September 30, 1996 was hit by delayed monsoons and power shortages.
It said in a statement the abnormal delay in the arrival of monsoons at Nagda affected VSF production for 46 days during June and July 1996.
VSF production at Nagda was lower at 46,789 tonnes in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March), from 51,692 tonnes during the corresponding period last year.

"To ensure that such delays in the arrival of monsoon do not affect the VSF operations at Nagda in future, a new dam adequate to hold three months water requirement was commissioned in May 1996," Grasim said.
"The additional storage will ensure that there is no shortage of water in future for the company's operations at Nagda."
Grasim said VSF production at Mavoor was also lower at 5,114 tonnes in the first half of 1996/97 against 8,025 tonnes a year ago due to a power cut.

"The VSF production at Mavoor initially got affected due to a 100 percent power cut imposed by Kerala State Electricity Board due to a paucity of water in the Hydel reservoirs and, later on, on account of excessive rains causing heavy floods," the firm said.
It said VSF production at Harihar was marginally higher at 17,751 tonnes against 16,829 tonnes.
Grasim said production of caustic soda was lower at 52,795 tonnes against 57,752 tonnes.

Cement output was also affected due to severe power cuts and interruptions in power supply by the Madhya Pradesh State Electricity Board. Production at Jawad was lower at 1,064,423 tonnes against 1,198,834 tonnes.
Cement production at two new units of Raipur and Shambhupra was at 955,770 tonnes against 232,293 a year ago.

"While the aggregate production of all cement units was higher at 2,020,193 tonnes against 1,431,127 tonnes in the corresponding period last year, the margins were adversely affected... due to a glut situation prevailing in northern India during July to September 1996 and considerable increase in the prices of steam, coal, power and freight," Grasim said.
